rules.classification: Spectroscopic classes and alert or messenger labels are different definitions and are not compared; two active classes differ when neither label refines the other (for example 'SN Ia' and 'SN Ia-91T' agree); an earlier value from the same provider is a revision.
rules.host: Two proposed hosts agree when their names match after case and spacing are ignored or one name is among the other's NED cross-identifications; otherwise they are an identity ambiguity. Association probabilities are not computed.
rules.photometry: Only exactly compatible photometry (same epoch, band, system, method, calibration and direct/difference state, two or more providers) is compared. The limiting magnitude or flux that a provider reports alongside a detection is that epoch's detection threshold, not a non-detection, and is not compared with the detection; a detection brighter than another provider's non-detection limit at the same epoch is a status conflict. A group is listed only when it is still inconsistent under these rules; at most 10 groups per event, most significant first.
rules.position: Two positions with no stated uncertainty are inconsistent when they are more than 2 arcsec apart; when one states an error radius, the separation is compared with 3 times that radius.
rules.redshift: Two redshifts with no stated uncertainty are inconsistent when they differ by more than 0.005 (about 1,500 km/s); transient and host redshifts are different definitions and are listed, not compared; host redshifts of differently named hosts are an identity ambiguity.
rules.revision: A retracted row, or a superseded row of the same provider whose value differs beyond the property's rule, is a revision or retraction; a revision within the rule is consistent; the earlier value stays visible.
rules.sigma: Two values that both state an uncertainty are inconsistent when they differ by more than 3 combined standard deviations (uncertainties added in quadrature; a stated position error radius is treated as one standard deviation).
